# Fluentic i18n: LLM guide

Fluentic i18n v0.1.0-beta.2 translates natural source messages without application-defined keys. React/Vite is the primary SPA path.

## Load only what the task needs

- Wrap or review user-facing text: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/messages.txt
- Install and configure a React/Vite SPA: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/setup-vite.txt
- React updates, language switching, and subscriptions: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/react-runtime.txt
- Extract, translate, review, and merge catalogs: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/translation-flow.txt
- Build-time compiler behavior and restrictions: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/compiler.txt
- Complete minimal SPA example: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/react-vite-example.txt
- Compact API reference: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/llms/api.txt

Human documentation: https://fluenticstack.com/i18n/docs/intro/

## Rules for modifying application source

1. Import the named `t` object from `@fluentic/i18n`. Do not rename or wrap it.
2. Wrap user-facing UI copy, accessibility text, labels, placeholders, titles, validation errors, toasts, empty states, and loading/error messages.
3. Do not translate user data, API content, IDs, URLs, CSS classes, analytics names, protocol strings, or developer-only logs.
4. Keep source messages as static literals. Use ICU params instead of concatenation or JavaScript interpolation.
5. Use `t.jsx(message, params?)` for translated React content. It updates itself.
6. Use `t.text(message, params?)` when a string is required.
7. When React renders `t.text()`, choose one subscription:
   - `I18nState.use()` rerenders the whole component; use for convenience or many language-dependent values.
   - `t.jsx(() => element)` reruns only one element callback; use as a performance escape hatch for translated string props.
8. A `t.jsx(() => element)` callback must return one React element. Do not call hooks inside it. Nested messages are extracted and compiled normally.
9. Use `t.msg()` for reusable messages and typed parameter schemas.
10. Use `t.context()` when identical source wording has different meanings. Use `t.note()` for translator guidance and `t.meta()` for JSON metadata.

## Core patterns

```tsx
import { t } from '@fluentic/i18n';

// Reactive React content
<button>{t.jsx('Save changes')}</button>

// String prop; parent component must subscribe with I18nState.use()
<input placeholder={t.text('Search projects')} />

// Targeted string-prop boundary; parent does not rerender for language changes
t.jsx(() => (
  <input placeholder={t.text('Search projects')} />
))

// Reusable, typed message
const greeting = t.msg('Welcome back, {name}!', { name: String });
t.jsx(greeting, { name: user.name });

// Same wording, different meaning, with translator guidance
t.context('checkout')
  .note('Primary payment action')
  .meta({ screen: 'checkout' })
  .jsx('Continue');
```

## Required validation after an i18n change

```sh
pnpm i18n:extract
pnpm i18n:merge
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

Never edit generated `merged.*` catalogs directly. Edit `manual.jsonl`, then run merge.
